title: Acropolis Hill
description: The ancient citadel rises above Athens, a timeless reminder of classical Greek civilization. The marble structures catch the Mediterranean light, standing as silent witnesses to thousands of years of history.

title: Acropolis View
description: From below, the Acropolis dominates the Athens skyline. The ancient temples and theaters create a silhouette against the blue sky, connecting the modern city to its classical past.

title: Arch of Hadrian
description: This Roman triumphal arch marks the boundary between the ancient and classical Athens. Built in 131 AD, it stands as a gateway between different eras of the city's long history.

title: Hadrian's Library
description: The remains of this Roman-era library stand as testament to Athens' importance as a center of learning. The Corinthian columns and architectural fragments hint at the grandeur that once was.

title: Roman Columns
description: Ancient Roman columns rise from the earth, their weathered surfaces telling stories of centuries past. These architectural fragments connect modern Athens to its classical heritage.

title: Temple of Aphaia
description: This well-preserved Doric temple on the island of Aegina showcases the architectural brilliance of ancient Greece. The marble columns and pediments demonstrate classical proportions at their finest.

title: Temple of Apollo in Corinth
description: Seven massive columns remain standing from this once-magnificent temple. Built in the 6th century BC, it was one of the most important temples in ancient Greece, dedicated to the god of music and prophecy.

title: Temple of Hephaestus
description: The best-preserved ancient Greek temple in Athens, dedicated to the god of craftsmanship and fire. Its Doric columns and detailed metopes showcase the mastery of classical architecture.
